notes: mc RATES (checked; the prefetch's market keys are kept, none written here): 10-year Treasury 4.96% on 2026-10-22 (FRED DGS10, pf_fred_dgs10). Re-read from FRED on 2026-10-26: the last published print is 2026-10-22 at 4.96%, after 5.13% on 2026-10-21 (a 17 bp one-day fall; the 2026-10-23 print was not yet published); raw copy in gather/raw_macro/fred__DGS10_recheck.csv. Implied ERP 4.20% (Damodaran update of 2026-10-01, treasury 5.29% on that date, pf_erp_implied) is the newest monthly update on or before 2026-10-26, so it is kept, not refetched. mc GEOGRAPHY: revenue is designated by the location of the direct customer's headquarters, not the end customer or the shipping location (10-K and 10-Q, pf_10k_20260225, pf_10q_20260826). Q2 FY2027 (three months to 2026-07-26): United States 62.4%, Taiwan 28.0%, China including Hong Kong 8.2%, other 1.3% of 96,221 million; H1 FY2027: United States 69.6%, Taiwan 21.9%, China 7.0%. China including Hong Kong was 20.2% of revenue in FY2024, 19.2% in FY2025, 9.1% in FY2026 (facts mc_share_cn_*). Taiwan-headquartered customers are mostly ODMs and system builders: the company estimates 76% of their FY2026 Data Center revenue was attributed to end customers in the United States and Europe (mc_tw_dc_endcust_us_eu_fy26), so the Taiwan row is largely US and European demand routed through Taiwan. Long-lived assets (property and equipment) at 2026-01-25: United States 49.4%, Taiwan 31.0%, Israel 14.2%, other 5.5% of 10,383 million (mc_lla_*); Taiwan doubled from 1,481 million a year earlier. Gap: no long-lived-asset table in the 10-Q, so the latest value is 2026-01-25; the composition of China-headquartered revenue by product (gaming, workstation, networking, other) is not disclosed in the filings read, so how much of the 7,880 million in Q2 FY2027 is data center is not known (the 10-Q and the CFO commentary say Hopper shipments to China were under 1% of Data Center revenue, pf_10q_20260826, pf_rel_20260826_2).

mc EXPOSURE china_export_controls (sized): US licence requirements and the PRC's own restrictions. April 2025 licence requirement on the H20 led to a 4.5 billion USD charge in Q1 FY2026; from August 2025 licences for H20 were granted but the PRC restricted sales; from February 2026 licences for small H200 amounts, sales again restricted by the PRC, a 0.4 billion USD H200 inventory and purchase-obligation charge in H1 FY2027, shipments under 1% of Data Center revenue in Q2 FY2027; the 10-Q says the company is effectively foreclosed from China's data center compute market and that this lost opportunity helps competitors build ecosystems, with a material and adverse impact unless it returns with a system approved by both governments. The outlook assumes no China data center compute revenue (pf_rel_20260826_1, pf_rel_20260826_2); the Hopper shipments under 1% figure is in the 10-Q and in the CFO commentary (pf_rel_20260826_2). Revenue still exposed in the geography row: China including Hong Kong 8.2% of Q2 FY2027 revenue (7,880 million, mc_rev_cn_q2fy27), 9.1% of FY2026 (mc_share_cn_fy26); the data-center-compute part is already out of the guidance, so the bear mechanism for that part is the further loss of the non-compute China revenue and a write-down on any Hopper inventory (sized by the charges above), and the bull mechanism is a return (not assumed) [evidence: pf_10q_20260826, pf_10k_20260225, pf_rel_20260826_1].

mc EXPOSURE china_competition_regulator (sized only for the product line; the China share of it is a gap): on 2025-09-15 China's antitrust regulator published a preliminary finding that the company's compliance with US export controls (degraded products for China) breached the terms of China's approval of the Mellanox acquisition; possible penalties and restrictions on the networking business in China (10-Q risk factor). Networking revenue was 31,376 million USD in FY2026 = 14.5% of revenue (10-K end-market table); the China part of networking is not disclosed. The PRC also encourages buyers to choose China-based competitors and issued an Action Plan on performance-per-watt standards for data centers. Penalty size: hypothesis, not sized [evidence: pf_10q_20260826, pf_10k_20260225].

mc EXPOSURE taiwan_south_korea_supply (share unsized: the company does not give the share of wafers, packaging or memory sourced there): the 10-K and 10-Q say the supply chain is mainly concentrated in Asia and the business depends on reliable supply from overseas partners, especially in Taiwan and South Korea; foundries TSMC and Samsung, memory from SK Hynix, Micron and Samsung, CoWoS packaging, assembly by Hon Hai, Wistron and Fabrinet; a limited number and geographic concentration of suppliers is a named risk; geopolitical tensions where partners are located could have a material adverse impact (10-K). Sized markers: long-lived assets in Taiwan 31.0% (mc_lla_share_tw_fy26); Taiwan-headquartered customers 28.0% of Q2 FY2027 revenue (mc_share_tw_q2fy27); supply and capacity commitments rose from 119 billion USD at the previous quarter to 279 billion USD at 2026-07-26, mainly memory and manufacturing facilities for data center systems, some cancelable or reschedulable (10-Q Note 10). A bear mechanism for a supply disruption is therefore hypothesis in size (share of supply unknown) but the cost of a demand or rule change on commitments is sized at up to 279 billion USD gross [evidence: pf_10k_20260225, pf_10q_20260826].

mc EXPOSURE tariffs (sized narrowly): Section 232 proclamation of 2026-01-14 imposed a 25% tariff on certain advanced computing chips such as the H200 and MI325X, with an exemption for chips imported to support the US technology supply chain buildout, and said broader tariffs on semiconductors and derivatives may follow (mc_wh_232_20260114, a search excerpt of the fact sheet, not the full text). The 10-Q says H200s shipped under the China licence programme go through US inspection and so bear the 25% tariff, which the company has not been able to pass to customers and does not expect to; tariffs are also a named cost-of-revenue item. Sized exposure today: H200 shipments under 1% of Data Center revenue; a broader tariff is not sized (hypothesis) [evidence: pf_10q_20260826, mc_wh_232_20260114].

mc EXPOSURE us_rules_and_bills (unsized, hypothesis): the replacement for the rescinded AI Diffusion rule has no stated scope or date; the GAIN AI Act passed the Senate within the NDAA in October 2025 and would limit the administration's flexibility on export rules; the Remote Access Security Act could bar cloud services to companies whose ultimate parent is headquartered in China; the USG may also add controls on networking products, gaming GPUs, chip tracking or throttling, and license conditions on foreign GPU-cluster services (10-Q). The French Competition Authority is questioning whether gaming and data center GPUs are separate product categories, which may affect export controls on gaming products in France and Europe (10-Q). A substantial portion of products is warehoused in and distributed from Hong Kong, which export controls could disrupt (10-Q) [evidence: pf_10q_20260826].

mc EXPOSURE antitrust_other_jurisdictions (unverified, hypothesis): press from 2024 reports a US Department of Justice antitrust inquiry with a subpoena, and a secondary French site describes the French competition authority as near a statement of objections with a maximum penalty of 10% of global revenue; the 10-Q names only the French authority's GPU-category question and the Chinese regulator's Mellanox finding, so the DOJ, EU and French items are leads, not facts; no primary document read and none registered as a source.

mc EXPOSURE israel (sized): about 6,000 employees in Israel mainly supporting networking R&D, operations and sales; employees have at times been on extended military duty with limited disruption so far (10-K); long-lived assets in Israel 14.2% (mc_lla_share_il_fy26) [evidence: pf_10k_20260225].

mc EXPOSURE hugging_face_regulatory (sized by price, outcome unsized): the pending acquisition needs regulatory approvals; the company's own risk factor says governments may restrict AI models including open-source models, many of the popular ones originate in China, and any restriction on supporting models derived from China could materially affect Hugging Face and the company [evidence: mc_sec_8k_20260902].

mc NEWS 2026-09-03 (event 2026-09-02): Form 8-K Item 8.01. Definitive agreement to acquire Hugging Face, Inc., an open-source model and dataset platform: about 11.9 billion USD to Hugging Face stockholders, subject to adjustments, plus an equity-based retention programme of up to about 1.0 billion USD (total about 12.9 billion USD); expected to close in the first half of calendar 2027 subject to customary conditions including regulatory approvals; the company commits to keep the platform open and to support other silicon vendors. Press coverage (TechRadar, Adweek and others) repeats the 8-K and is not independent evidence [evidence: mc_sec_8k_20260902].

mc NEWS 2026-08-17: Form 8-K Items 1.01, 2.03, 7.01 (filed before the 10-Q of 2026-08-26, after the quarter end 2026-07-26). Multi-year partnership with SB Energy for the PORTS campus in Pike County, Ohio; residual value guaranties on leases of about 4.25 GW of IT load, cumulative payment cap 105 billion USD, tenant an affiliate of OpenAI, payment obligations conditioned on ready-for-service expected from 2028, with OpenAI to reimburse and indemnify the company for amounts paid; optional credit support for about 3.8 GW more at the company's sole discretion. Also from the 10-Q: memorandums of understanding in August 2026 with capital providers for financing platforms meant to mobilize more than 500 billion USD of third-party capital, with optional limited residual-value support (financing exposure belongs to the funding and dilution review) [evidence: mc_sec_8k_20260817, pf_10q_20260826].

mc NEWS FILINGS CHECK: SEC submissions (refreshed by the prefetch on 2026-10-26) list, after the 10-Q of 2026-08-26, exactly one company 8-K (2026-09-03, Item 8.01, Hugging Face); the other filings are insider Forms 3, 4, 4/A and 144 (2026-08-31 to 2026-10-13, not read: insider sales are not in this lane's scope) and an N-PX. No 8-K or other periodic report is dated after 2026-09-03, and Q3 FY2027 (quarter ending 2026-10-25) has not been reported. Earlier 8-Ks in the year (2026-06-18 notes offering, 2026-06-24 Item 5.07 vote, 2026-06-28 Item 5.02, 2026-05-08 and 2026-04-27 Item 5.02, 2026-03-02 Item 5.02) pre-date the latest 10-Q and are left to the documents lane.

mc NEWS WEB SEARCH RESULT: eight web searches and one fetch for press after 2026-08-26 on export controls and China, tariffs, antitrust, supply and general company news returned only items from January to March 2026 or earlier, apart from coverage of the Hugging Face deal. Nothing dated after the latest 10-Q was found on export rules, China, tariffs or antitrust, which is absence of search results, not evidence that nothing happened. Leads kept as unverified background, none registered as a source: (a) January 2026 Reuters report (via Yahoo Finance, 2026-01-14) that Chinese customs agents were told not to allow H200 chips in, consistent with the 10-Q statement that the PRC restricted H200 sales; (b) March 2026 GTC statements that licences and purchase orders existed for China H200 and production had restarted, which the 10-Q overtakes (shipments under 1% of Data Center revenue); (c) March to April 2026 reports from single secondary sources of HBM4 supply shortfalls and Rubin ramp slippage, with figures such as a 2026 Rubin production target cut from 2 million to 1.5 million units that no primary document confirms: hypothesis only, to be checked against the Q3 FY2027 call.
gaps: No press dated after 2026-08-26 found on export rules, China, tariffs or antitrust (search returned January to March 2026 items only); the status of Beijing's stance on H200 imports in September and October 2026 is unconfirmed beyond the 10-Q statement of 2026-08-26.

Share of wafer, packaging and memory supply from Taiwan and South Korea is not disclosed in the filings read, so the Taiwan supply-disruption mechanism is a hypothesis in size; sized markers only (31.0% of long-lived assets, 28.0% of Q2 FY2027 revenue by customer headquarters, 279 billion USD supply commitments).

Composition of China-headquartered revenue by product (7,880 million USD in Q2 FY2027) is not disclosed in the filings read; the China share of networking revenue (Mellanox remedy exposure) is not disclosed.
Long-lived assets by country exist only for 2026-01-25 (10-K); the 10-Q does not repeat the table.
DOJ, EU and French antitrust items are secondary-press leads only, no primary document read.
Section 232 proclamation read through a search excerpt of the White House fact sheet, not the proclamation text; broader semiconductor tariffs are only 'may follow'.
Insider Forms 3, 4 and 144 filed 2026-08-31 to 2026-10-13 not read (outside this lane's keys).
